nodes.label: The Selfless Caregiver
nodes.description: Story that my life and needs are secondary to caring for others.
summary: Moved back to childhood home to care for mother without being asked
Assumed she could handle everything because she is a nurse
Believes taking care of others means completely sacrificing her own life

quotes.text: At work, I clock out. At home, there's no clocking out.

nodes.label: The Invisible Anger
nodes.description: Carrying deep resentment while always saying yes and keeping the peace.
summary: Feels furious at brother Daniel for assuming she would take on caregiving
Keeps anger hidden to protect the family peace and her mother
Suffers in silence because she believes she is not allowed to complain

quotes.text: And I said okay. I always say okay.

nodes.label: The Burden Of Obligation
nodes.description: Feeling trapped by family duty with no end in sight.
summary: Compares her current life to her mother's history of working two jobs without complaint
Wonders how many years caregiving will last and feels guilty for the thought
Grieves the loss of her partner, apartment, and freedom in Sacramento

quotes.text: And I feel so selfish for even thinking that.

nodes.label: Not Needing Anything
nodes.description: Belief that having personal needs or limits is unacceptable.
summary: Lists being patient, never snapping, and keeping the house clean as requirements
Realized aloud that expecting herself to have zero needs is unrealistic

quotes.text: Being patient. Never snapping. Keeping the house clean. Keeping her happy. Not needing anything.

nodes.label: Expressing Anger Causes Damage
nodes.description: Assumption that speaking up will cause everyone around her to fall apart.
summary: Fears brother Daniel would get defensive if she shared her true feelings
Worries her mother would pick up on tension and make things worse

quotes.text: If I told him I was angry, he'd get defensive, and then Mom would pick up on the tension

nodes.label: My Life Counts Less
nodes.description: Implicit rule that unmarried people without children must sacrifice their lives.
summary: Notes that because she lacks a spouse or kids, her life was easily packed up
Feels hurt that nobody asked before thrusting the caregiving role onto her

quotes.text: Like I don't have a life because I'm not married and don't have kids

nodes.label: Numbing With Wine And TV
nodes.description: Using alcohol and television at night to cope with relentless exhaustion.
summary: Relies on two to three glasses of wine after her mother is asleep
Recognizes it as her only method of self-care and finding quiet time

quotes.text: Honestly? Wine and TV after she's asleep. That's my thing.

nodes.label: Hiding Emotional Pain
nodes.description: Crying in secret and suppressing grief to avoid burdening others.
summary: Runs bathroom water so her mother cannot hear her cry
Has not allowed herself to grieve her ended relationship due to lack of time

quotes.text: I go in the bathroom and run the water so she can't hear me.

nodes.label: Perpetual Compliance
nodes.description: Instantly agreeing to demands and suppressing disagreements to keep peace.
summary: Agreed immediately when family assumed she would take on caregiving
Acknowledges a lifelong pattern of always saying okay

quotes.text: And I said okay. I always say okay.

nodes.label: Rest And Restoration
nodes.description: Longing for physical and mental relief from constant demands.
summary: Suffers from bone-tired exhaustion and severely disrupted sleep patterns
Yearns for the quiet moment of putting everything down at night

quotes.text: It's like... I can finally put everything down.

nodes.label: Recognition And Being Seen
nodes.description: Desire to be consulted and valued as a person with her own life.
summary: Expressed deep hurt over not being asked before her life was uprooted
Articulated the painful feeling that her existence didn't count

nodes.label: Autonomy And Personal Time
nodes.description: Yearning for genuine personal time independent of caregiving chores.
summary: Imagines having one day a week that is truly hers, not used for errands
Wants space to reclaim a life outside of her mother's illness

quotes.text: I'd have one day a week that was mine. Actually mine.

nodes.label: Family Loyalty And Care
nodes.description: Deep commitment to protecting and looking after her mother.
summary: Moved across cities and rearranged her entire life to keep her mother safe
Expresses genuine love for her mother despite the crushing caregiver fatigue

quotes.text: I don't mean I want her to die. I love her.

nodes.label: Authenticity And Honesty
nodes.description: The desire to speak her truth and communicate openly with family.
summary: Expressed a deep wish to be able to talk honestly with her brother Daniel
Felt a sense of relief after admitting her true feelings in the session

quotes.text: And I'd be able to talk to Daniel without wanting to scream.

edges.explanation: The belief that she should have no needs directly fuels her role as the selfless caregiver.
Her constant compliance and automatic agreement trap her deeper into the caregiver role.
Believing her life counts less justifies the total sacrifice demanded by her caregiver role.
Fear of causing damage prevents her from expressing her hidden anger.
Always saying yes to others builds up the silent rage she carries.
The overwhelming obligation of duty stems directly from her dedication to caregiving.
Numbing with wine is her coping mechanism for the relentless exhaustion of caregiving.
Hiding her emotional pain allows her to maintain her exterior as a strong caregiver.
Her severe depletion of rest is a direct consequence of continuous caregiving without breaks.
Not being asked or considered as a person triggers her intense resentment and anger.
Her lack of personal autonomy is the core pain point within her burden of obligation.
Her core value of family loyalty is what compelled her into the caregiver narrative.
Her value of honesty directly contrasts with her suppressed anger toward her brother.
